findings.evidence: By the definition at AlongCurve/Basic.lean:107-111, `derivWithin (extChartAt I x ∘ fun _ ↦ x) s t = 0`, so the `christoffelMap ... (derivWithin ...)` term vanishes by linearity. The remaining `derivWithin (sectionCoord ...)` term is the chart image of `derivWithin V`, and `symmL` at `x` inverts `continuousLinearMapAt` there (as used in `alongCurveWithin_smul`, line 215).
findings.fix: Add `alongCurveWithin_const (x) (V : 𝕜 → TangentSpace I x) : alongCurveWithin cov (fun _ ↦ x) V s t = derivWithin V s t` and its `alongCurve` version. Get the constant and affine cases from it by `simp`, or drop them (the affine case is used only at Jacobi/Exponential.lean:121).
findings.issue: `alongCurveWithin_const_const`/`alongCurve_const_const` (constant field) and `alongCurve_const_add_smul` (field `v + q • w`) are special cases of one fact: along a constant curve, `alongCurveWithin cov (fun _ ↦ x) V s t = derivWithin V s t` for any `V : 𝕜 → TangentSpace I x`. The affine case is rebuilt from `alongCurve_add`/`alongCurve_smul` with hand-made differentiability side goals.

findings.issue: `sectionCoord_const` covers only a constant field along a constant curve. The general lemma above needs the version for an arbitrary field along the constant curve.

summary: The Jacobi/exp statements sit at the natural level, but the new constant-curve covariant-derivative lemmas are special cases of one general identity (covariant derivative along a constant curve = ordinary derivative of the field), and the affine case re-derives it by hand.
